materiality: A fully imported remote HiSparse/NIXL prefix still needs a writable final resident page for last-token replay; treating every imported full block as host-only can expose missing or uninitialized GPU state on decode continuation.
The upstream repair explicitly restores the tail page, tracks pending restore lifetime and exercises exact full/partial block boundaries, aborts and refcounts.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact vLLM/NIXL source, image, block size, connector configuration, model/tokenizer and accelerator topology.
Run the known-bad predecessor and candidate at token counts 1, 15, 16, 17, 31, 32, 33 and 127; prove final-page restore, last-token replay and prefix-cache visibility semantics.
Exercise abort during pending restore, transfer failure, request cancellation, restart and refcount cleanup; missing hardware is UNAVAILABLE, not PASS.
Preserve rollback to the incumbent exact serving path and require output/logit parity before performance claims.

materiality: MLP synchronization can represent an originally IDLE DP rank as a dummy zero-token EXTEND batch; logits pruning must retain the original idle semantic or it can index a nonexistent last token and crash.
This is a distributed serving correctness/availability boundary rather than routine batching cleanup.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact SGLang source/image, DP/TP topology, model and MLP-sync configuration.
Use a known-bad zero-token idle-rank fixture and candidate fixture; require zero logits rows on the idle rank while padded execution state remains valid for attention/MLP synchronization.
Exercise mixed idle/active ranks, logprob on/off, speculative modes, repeated empty batches, cancellation and worker restart with no cross-rank output contamination.
Keep every unexercised topology UNQUALIFIED and preserve rollback.

materiality: Exact-token preprocessing assumed PIL image height/width attributes even when CUDA decoding yields CHW tensors, causing a valid multimodal input path to fail before token accounting.
Token-count drift at the processor boundary can change context accounting and therefore must be qualified independently of model quality.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact SGLang source/image, model/processor, decoder backend and input image bytes.
Run the predecessor and candidate on equivalent PIL and tensor-backed JPEG/image inputs; require identical intended dimensions, image-token counts and model-visible prompt structure.
Exercise grayscale/RGB, non-square dimensions, malformed tensors, CPU/CUDA decode availability and fallback without silently re-encoding unsupported inputs.
Measure latency only after preprocessing and output parity pass; preserve incumbent fallback.

materiality: The Transformers backend used by vLLM could compute video token counts through the wrong patch-count API and merge-size path across multiple VLM processors.
The upstream change is explicitly Part 1, so it is a bounded token-accounting correction and not evidence of complete video support.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact Transformers/vLLM source, model, processor, video processor, decoder, sampled video bytes and generation configuration.

Use a known-bad predecessor plus candidate to compare processor-declared video tokens against independently derived frame/patch/merge calculations for representative durations, resolutions and merge_size overrides.
Exercise truncation/context limits, multiple videos, malformed metadata, decoder fallback and server restart; prove prompt-token accounting matches actual model input.
Keep all models/processors not explicitly exercised UNQUALIFIED and do not claim Part 2 or complete video parity.

materiality: A single server-invalid .eval_results YAML placeholder could raise in the Hub parser and discard every otherwise valid evaluation entry in the repository.
SZL treats evaluation and proof records as evidence-bearing inputs, so fault isolation must preserve valid entries without converting the invalid entry into success by omission.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact huggingface_hub source/wheel and the exact eval-result response fixture consumed by SZL tooling.

Known-bad control: one valid entry plus one server error placeholder must demonstrate predecessor all-entry loss; candidate must retain the valid entry and surface the invalid filename/error as a non-success diagnostic.

Exercise multiple invalid entries, malformed valid-looking entries, empty response and ordering; downstream proof aggregation must preserve unknown/invalid status and may never compute a complete PASS from the surviving subset alone.
Route measured proof changes through the existing a11oy-net owner only after exact-source qualification; preserve v1.32 rollback and PR #179 boundaries.

materiality: AsyncGRPO now executes synchronous tools in a bounded thread pool and accepts asynchronous tools, preventing a slow synchronous tool from blocking unrelated in-flight generation.
The concurrency change introduces explicit thread-safety, shared-state, cancellation and side-effect ordering obligations that are not covered by #76's earlier adapter-sync scope.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact TRL source/environment, AsyncGRPO configuration, vLLM runtime and synthetic non-secret tool implementations.
Exercise synchronous, asynchronous, slow, failing and missing tools; require model-emitted per-turn result order, bounded max_inflight_tasks concurrency and responsive event-loop progress.

Use shared-state race fixtures plus cancellation, timeout, rollout restart, trainer stop/backpressure and retry scenarios; assert no duplicate consequential side effects and no orphan executor work crosses rollout identity.
Retain #76 adapter-version/staleness/shared-path gates independently; no tool-concurrency success transfers adapter-sync qualification or authorizes production effectors.

alignmentDependency.note: Fresh HF runtime and product reads report the protected A11oy SHA, while proof remains dated. Different observation windows are not combined into a whole-chain PASS.
